answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independently checked tasks reveal fraud. This makes a sybil attack costly: an attacker must lock capital for every fake identity and risks losing it, rather than creating accounts for free. The bond can sit in a velvet-glove escrow, while a vine of linked task audits exposes coordinated submissions; a glacier-slow withdrawal delay gives auditors time to flag them.
